os.Mkdir with mode 0700 is exclusive and refuses an existing final component, links included; the name is built only from a validated hex id; cleanup checks directory identity. Predictability and escaped processes fall within L2 and L3.
A per-attempt path is smaller than telling the session a new path, which would alter what provenance verifies, and adds no extension point. It stops working when TMPDIR differs (L1).

findings.action: The manual (all four copies), spec technical risks (line 79) and the error at review_dispatch.go:2082 say that removing a directory left by an unfinished cleanup restores resume. PlanReviewResume refuses a predecessor with incomplete cleanup first (review_run_continuity.go:405-407), so it does not.

PlanReviewHandoff does not check that the attempt's runtime directory is free. With a leftover or foreign directory, the handoff claims the predecessor (review_dispatch.go:746), fails at :809, and the interrupted run can no longer be resumed.

The claim lookup and the directory check are not atomic: a concurrent resume that loses the race can be told to remove a live run's directory instead of receiving pending. Established by reading, not reproduced.
The delegated-run-continuity integration pattern RunContinuity selects neither new regression test, and no matrix pattern names them.
The test isolates with TMPDIR, which Windows ignores; with a fixed attempt id it would use the real temp directory and could leave a link there that fails later runs.
